articles.body: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned immigrants and visa applicants not to fall for businesses, websites, or individuals that claim they can secure faster approvals for visas, Green Cards, or work permits in exchange for a fee. According to the agency, such promises are often signs of immigration scams. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) USCIS wrote, “ IT'S A SCAM: Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government. They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee.”USCIS warns against false promisesThe agency said applicants should be cautious of anyone claiming to have a special relationship with the US government or USCIS that can influence immigration decisions. USCIS notes that immigration benefits are processed through official procedures and warns that no private individual or organisation can guarantee a specific outcome or accelerated processing simply because of claimed government connections.USCIS also stressed that applicants do not need a representative to file immigration forms and may submit applications on their own. Those seeking assistance should work only with qualified attorneys or accredited representatives recognised by the US Department of Justice.Be aware that scammers:•Try to confuse you by complicating the immigration process;•Use social media, email, or phone calls to conduct their attacks; and•Impersonate government officials to manipulate the victim into giving out personal information.How applicants can protect themselvesAs part of its anti-fraud guidance, USCIS encourages applicants to verify information through official government websites, obtain written agreements for any legal services, keep copies of immigration forms and records, and be wary of offers that sound too good to be true. The agency maintains an online resource to help immigrants identify and avoid common scams and fraud schemes.Be cautious of:•Emails that look legitimate, but are sent by people you don’t know;•Emails with typos and incorrect spellings;•E-mails that do not end in .gov and end in (.net, .org, .com, or .info for example)•Suspicious emails you don’t normally receive;•Offers of assistance to expedite your case for money;•Promises of a quick benefit; and•Downloading or opening attachments from senders you don’t recognize.; and•Requests from USCIS to transfer money to an individual or pay fees other than through your myUSCIS accountYou use AI every day. articles.title: Cowboys Defense Must Prove its Meeting Meant Something
articles.summary: The Cowboys defense held an honest meeting after its latest loss. Now Dallas must turn accountability into better execution against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
The Cowboys defense has discussed what it wants to become. Against the Green Bay Packers, it must begin showing whether those conversations can change its performance.

Following the Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay, Dallas' defensive players took time to examine their standards and responsibilities. DeMarvion Overshown described the Monday, October 12 meeting as an opportunity to evaluate themselves and discuss how they could hep one another.

That conversation offers a meaningful starting point. However, its value will depend on whether Dallas communicates more clearly, handles assignments more consistently and prevent manageable plays from becoming costly mistakes.

Cowboys Defense Takes an Honest Look at its Standards

According to Overshown, the defense wrote its expectations on a board and reviewed them individually. Players considered whether their performances matched those expectations and what they needed from their teammates during preparation and games.

"What can I do to help you?" was one of the questions Overshown used to explain the discussion. His account emphasized cooperation and accountability rather than panic or accusations.

That distinction matters. A productive meeting should give players specific responsibilities they can carry into practice. General promises about effort provide little direction unless teammates understand what must change and how to recognize improvement.

For Dallas, accountability should also extend beyond the players nearest the ball when a players breaks down. Coaches and defenders must identify how positioning, communication and execution contribution to the result before deciding on a correction.

The Problems Requires More than Better Intentions

Through five games, Dallas ranked 31st in total defense , allowing 395.4 yards per game. That performance helps explain the urgency surrounding a team preparing for Green Bay with a 2-3 record.

The defensive breakdowns against Tampa Bay made another review necessary. The challenge now is to translate the discussion into preparation that produces reliable answers when opponents attack the same weaknesses.

Overshown identified mental errors as an obstacle and expressed confidence in the unit's potential. That confidence represents a player's assessment, rather than evidence that the defense has already turned a corner.

Against Green Bay, useful signs would include defenders getting aligned before the snap, maintaining their responsibilities against motion and finishing tackles after making initial contact. Those details offer a more practical measure of progress than emotional reactions after an isolated stop.

The response to a succesfull opposing drive will matter, too. Dallas must identify what worked against it, communicate a correction and execute that correction before the same problem damages another possession.

Coaching Support Must Produce Clearer Answers

The addition of Mike Pettine to the defensive staff gives Christian Parker another experienced resource. Pettine joined as a senior defensive assistant after previously working with both Parker and Brian Schottenheimer.

His arrival and the players' meeting address different parts of the same challenge. Coaches must provide assignments players can understand and execute, while defenders must communicate uncertainty before it becomes a mistake during a game.

Adding more instructions will not necessarily create better football. The staff should prioritize corrections that players can repeat under pressure, particularly when the offense changes its formation or forces a quick decision.

That responsibility also belongs to Schottenheimer as the leader of the entire team. He must ensure the defensive changes produce a coherent plan and that practice reinforces the standards players discussed

The Cowboys defense must play with urgency, toughness, and pride against Green Bay. After an honest conversation about their standards, players need to show that accountability through their effort: pursuing the ball, finishing tackles, and staying disciplined when the game gets difficult.

Emotion alone will not fix missed assignments, but Dallas needs its intensity and execution to match. Sunday offers this group an opportunity to back up its words with a performance that earns back some trust.

The players have examined what they expect from one another. Can they now make those expectations visible on the field?

articles.title: Popular Florida pro-am that attracts PGA Tour players, other pros turns 50
articles.summary: The Henry Tuten Gator Bowl Pro-Am reaches a milestone this year. And it will be a bittersweet celebration, without the tournament's namesake.
articles.body:
The Henry Tuten Gator Bowl Pro-Am reaches a milestone this year. And it will be a bittersweet celebration, without the tournament's namesake.

The holiday staple on the area's golf schedule will be Dec. 14-15 at the Sea Island Resort Seaside and Plantation Courses on St. Simons Island, Georgia. It will be the 50th playing of the tournament, which annually has attracted pros from the PGA Tour, PGA Tour Champions, LIV, Korn Ferry Tour, PGA Tour Americas and club professionals from Florida's First Coast and Georgia's Golden Isles.

Each pro is grouped with three amateurs and played 36 holes under a gross best ball.

Early commitments to play are PGA Tour winners Russell Knox, Keith Mitchell, Andrew Novak, Harold Varner III and Taylor Dickson.

Participants in the past have included World Golf Hall of Fame member Vijay Singh, Players Championship winners David Duval, Mark McCumber and Cameron Smith, and PGA Tour winners Len Mattiace, Kenny Perry, Frank Lickliter and Davis Thompson.

Tournament organizers will use its 50th anniversary to honor Tuten, who passed away in March at the age of 97. One of his legacies is more than $100,000 in charitable giving over the last six years to area golf-themed non-profits.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Eugenio Chacarra leads but Rory McIlroy fades before play halted
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra extends his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy loses ground before the third round is halted because of darkness.
articles.body:
DP World India Championship, round three leaderboard

14 E Chacarra (Spa) (11*); -12 J Luiten (Ned) (12*), A Hidalgo (Spa) (11*); -11 D Hillier (NZ) (14*), A Meronk (Pol) (11*), S Jamieson (Sco) (11*); -10 T McKibbin (NI) (14*), JC Ritchie (SA) (14*), T Clements (Eng) (12*), J Girrbach (Swi) (12*)

Selected others: -9 T Fleetwood (Eng); -8 R MacIntyre (Sco) (13*), D Bradbury (Eng); -7 S Lowry (Ire), L Canter (Eng); -6 P Reed (US) (13*), E Pepperell (Eng) (12*), M Armitage (Eng); -5 A Rai (Eng) (14*) -4 R McIlroy (NI) (15*); -2 J Rose (Eng) (11*)

*Denotes number of holes played before play ended on day one

Eugenio Chacarra extended his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy lost ground before the third round was halted because of darkness.

Spain's Chacarra led by one shot at 10 under after two rounds at the weather-hit event at Delhi Golf Club and sits two clear after 11 holes of his third round.

After successive rounds of 67, the 26-year-old birdied four of his opening seven holes to cement his place at the top as he bids to replace American Patrick Reed at the summit of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

Fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo and the Netherlands' Joost Luisten are his closest challengers at 12 under, with Scotland's Scott Jamieson a shot further back.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin is four adrift with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood five back after a four-under 68.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre is also well placed at eight under with five holes of his third round remaining.

However, McIlroy - who sits third in the Race to Dubai behind Reed and Chacarra - fell 10 shots off the lead after an erratic third round.

Having completed a bogey-free second-round 68 early on Saturday, the six-time major winner birdied his opening hole before dropping four shots in as many holes from the third.

After a birdie on the seventh, McIlroy made back-to-back bogeys on the ninth and 10th before sensationally holing out from the bunker for an eagle three at the 14th.

Reed played the first 13 holes of his third round to sit two shots ahead of McIlroy.

The 2018 Masters champion, who tops the Race to Dubai rankings after early-season victories in Dubai and Qatar, mixed five birdies and a bogey before holing his 150-yard approach shot for a spectacular eagle two at the fourth, having teed off at the 10th.

articles.title: Eugenio Chacarra, más líder en la India
articles.standfirst: Afianza su primer puesto, con dos golpes de ventaja sobre Joost Luiten y Ángel Hidalgo, durante una tercera ronda que quedó sin concluir
articles.summary: Afianza su primer puesto, con dos golpes de ventaja sobre Joost Luiten y Ángel Hidalgo, durante una tercera ronda que quedó sin concluir
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra se mantiene como líder del DP World India, en Nueva Delhi, tras una tercera jornada inconclusa por la falta de luz. El español se citó con el campo al alba (6.40 de la mañana) para, primero, acabar los hoyos pendientes de la segunda ronda. Tras otra tarjeta de 67 golpes se instaló en la cabeza en solitario con 10 bajo par, con uno de ventaja sobre el escocés Scott Jamieson. Poco después, arrancó el tercer recorrido. López-Chacarra completó 11 hoyos en los que firmó cuatro birdies (nueve en total en el día tras los cinco logrados en el desenlace de la segunda ronda) para colocarse 14 bajo par. Este resultado afianza su liderato. Amplía su ventaja sobre sus perseguidores: dos golpes sobre el holandés Joost Luiten (completó un hoyo más) y Ángel Hidalgo, que jugó en el mismo partido que Chacarra (Resultados). El DP World India ha ido a remolque desde el retraso de casi cinco horas en el inicio de la primera jornada. Este domingo Chacarra y el resto de jugadores volverán al campo para completar la tercera ronda desde las 06:35 de la mañana antes de afrontar los últimos 18 hoyos del torneo. Chacarra está más cerca de encabezar la clasificación Race to Dubai por delante del actual líder de la temporada, Patrick Reed, que pasó el corte con apuros, pero terminó el día seis bajo par, y de Rory McIlroy, que va cuatro abajo tras completar 15 hoyos en la tercera ronda con un +2. Eso sí, dejó un eagle desde el bunker en el 14. Si Chacarra gana este domingo lideraría la Race a falta de tres torneos (Corea, Abu Dhabi y Dubái) y estaría por primera vez entre los 40 mejores del ránking mundial lo que le aseguraría un billete para el Masters de Augusta. Al español se le da bien jugar en India. En 2025 ganó el Hero Indian Open y este año, en marzo, fue segundo.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Rory McIlroy drops 10 shots off the lead as Eugenio Chacarra moving into position for another big win
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy drops out of contention - 10 shots off leader Eugenio Chacarra - with Saturday's play suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round
articles.body:
Chacarra was leading by two strokes on 14 under when Saturday's play was suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round.

The Spaniard was four under for his round after 11 holes, having started out in the halfway lead after completing a second-round 67 early Saturday.

Joost Luiten was four under after 12 holes and Angel Hidalgo four under after 11 holes, with both players tied for second place on 12 under par.

Daniel Hillier, Adrian Meronk and Scott Jamieson were a further shot back.

Patrick Reed and McIlroy - battling with Chacarra for the season-long Race to Dubai title - were eight and 10 shots off the lead, respectively.

Chacarra earned one of the biggest wins of his career in India last year, triumphing at the Hero Indian Open - where he was playing on an invitation - to earn his full status on the European tour.

He had previously been on the LIV Golf circuit.

Play will restart at 6.35am local time on Sunday, with Chacarra needing to play the remaining seven holes of his third round as well as his entire final round.

articles.title: Bay Port, West De Pere, Notre Dame, Coleman earn top seeds in WIAA football playoffs
articles.summary: West De Pere, Notre Dame and Bay Port lead local teams into the WIAA playoffs while Green Bay West ends drought.
articles.body:
If there is going to be a rematch between the West De Pere and Bay Port football teams this season, it will come in the WIAA Division 1 state title game.

Both were a No. 1 seed when playoff brackets were released Oct. 17, two of four local teams to earn a top seed along with Green Bay Notre Dame in D2 and Coleman in D7.

First-round games are tentatively scheduled for Friday, Oct. 23, at 7 p.m. but are subject to change due to Game 1 of the World Series.

West De Pere (9-0) and Bay Port (8-1) are on opposite sides of the bracket, which means the teams could meet in the state championship game at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison next month.

The title games in seven divisions will be Nov. 19-20.

It would be the second straight season two local schools faced off on the big stage after West De Pere beat Green Bay Notre Dame in D2 in 2025.

The Phantoms defeated the Pirates this season for the third straight year and enter the postseason riding a 23-game winning streak.

Despite West De Pere losing one of the best quarterbacks in state history in Patrick Greisen to graduation along with head coach Chris Greisen, it hasn't missed much of a beat after being elevated to D1.

The Phantoms are the highest-ranked squad in the 32-team field, one year after they were the highest-ranked in D2.

They kick off what they hope is another run to state with an interesting opening round game against No. 8 seed Kimberly.

The Papermakers haven't been as dominant this season as past years, but they have been to the postseason every year since 2006 and won their most recent state title in 2022.

They started this season 0-3 – it included a 28-13 loss at Bay Port in Week 2 – but have won four of their last six.

Still, they will face a West De Pere team that has scored 35 or more points in every game while posting four shutouts.

Green Bay West football ends 30-year playoff drought

As for another dominating team, Notre Dame starts its quest to make a third straight title game by hosting No. 8 seed Germantown.

The Tritons were ranked second overall in the D2 field after a season in which they went 9-0 and set a local record for most points scored in the regular season with 511.

Notre Dame has won 36 of its last 37 games.

West De Pere, Bay Port, Notre Dame and Coleman were among 15 local teams to earn a playoff spot.

The only first-round game that features local teams squaring off comes in D2, where No. 3 Pulaski hosts No. 6 Ashwaubenon.

The Red Raiders beat the Jaguars 35-0 in Week 5 and have won each of the last 11 games in the series.

The most notable playoff team in the field might be Green Bay West, which is a No. 7 seed in D3 and will play at No. 2 Medford.

West is making its first playoff appearance since 1996 , breaking the longest postseason drought among Green Bay metro teams.

The Wildcats have won six games in a season for the first time since making the postseason 30 years ago.

"Hopefully, this leads to more kids coming out for football," West coach Drew Brusoe said. "Hopefully, it's more kids getting into our program at Franklin [Middle School]. They have been doing a great job. More kids, the better.

"Then, we have an opportunity to have three levels. The one goal this year was to make the playoffs. The other goal is getting three levels of football. JV2, freshmen, sophomores, playing against them. JV1, sophomores and juniors playing against equal competition. A lot of these kids have had to play on varsity since they were freshmen, or potentially sophomores. It took them two or three years to develop to what the team is now. There is a lot of talent here. Kids have worked their absolute tails off for it. I'm super proud of each and every one of them."

No. 6 Wrightstown at No. 3 Fuller Collegiate Academy

articles.title: Ferguson link has caused a 'real buzz' - McCann
articles.summary: Glentoran joint interim manager and former Glentoran captain Colin Nixon react to reports suggesting Duncan Ferguson is set to succeed Declan Devine as perma...
articles.body:
"I thought someone was maybe taking the hand but, listen, it's great."

Glentoran interim joint-manager Tim McCann's reaction to reports that former Everton striker Duncan Ferguson is set to succeed Declan Devine could be attributed to that of many Glens fans and those around the league upon hearing the news.

Devine departed the east Belfast club in mid-September after a slow start to the season with McCann - alongside Paddy McCourt - tasked with taking the team in the interim.

They have since steered the Glens to third in the table with four wins and a draw from six Irish Premiership fixtures.

Speaking after a 1-0 victory over Limavady, which was sealed with an injury-time goal from Daniel Larmour, McCann spoke of his excitement of Ferguson's potential arrival and the chance to work with the Scotsman, even if he didn't quite believe the initial reports.

"It's a change and it's caused a real buzz. It is great for the Irish League as well," McCann said on Sportsound.

"It's always difficult for managers coming from the outside, but listen, someone with that stature and that presence, that knowledge, that experience, as being a top pro and international player and all that comes with it, it'll be a vital experience and I think it'll be great."

If Ferguson, who won an FA Cup during his first spell with the Toffees, is to become Glentoran's fourth manager since January 2023, it would certainly represent "a left-field appointment" as former Glens captain Colin Nixon remarked.

Ferguson had two spells as caretaker manager and was also an assistant coach and first-team coach at Everton under various managers between 2019 and 2022.

He then left to take his first managerial role at League One Forest Green Rovers in January 2023, but won just one of his 18 games as they were relegated to League Two.

He then accepted a job at Scottish Championship side Inverness Caledonian Thistle in September 2023, but was sacked after the club went into administration in October 2024 and he has been out of management since.

Given his pedigree as a player in which he featured for Rangers and Newcastle as well as Everton, Nixon believes Glens fans should be excited, even if he does have reservations about Ferguson's Irish Premiership knowledge.

"What an exciting appointment, exciting for the league and exciting for Glentoran. It's quite unbelievable but exactly what Glentoran need at the minute," he said.

"In the back of my mind I worry what does he know about the league, but if he keeps the boys in the coaching positions they're in that will help."

Ferguson will have to pick up where McCann and McCourt left off and hit the ground running, with big league games against Ballymena, league leaders Coleraine and Carrick Rangers to come.

The good news is he has a talented squad to work with, including star striker Pat Hoban, who came off the bench on Saturday after an opening-day injury forced him to miss the next 10 league fixtures.

If Ferguson does take over at the Oval, it is set to be one of the most high-profile managerial appointments in Irish Premiership history and all eyes will be on the Scotsman to see if he can deliver the big trophies that have eluded the Glens in the last decade.
authors: Lauren McCann - BBC Sport NI Journalist

articles.title: Bears Defense Faces Nightmare Against Bijan Robinson
articles.summary: The Bears defense is hit with a massive injury crisis. Without Sweat, Edwards, and Odeyingbo, stopping the Falcons' Bijan Robinson will be a massive challeng...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears defense is heading into a total nightmare for Sunday's game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. After that 31-7 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers on October 11, the injury list just keeps growing. It feels like the defensive unit is falling apart right before the Atlanta Falcons arrive.

The situation is dire. According to Sports Illustrated , the team lost three vital edge-rushers and linebackers during the past week. Montez Sweat is currently serving a two-game suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy. On top of that, T.J. Edwards is out because he hurt his hamstring during the loss at Lambeau Field. Dayo Odeyingbo is also sidelined with a quadriceps injury, per Sports Illustrated.

Losing these guys makes stopping Bijan Robinson nearly impossible. Robinson is a monster lately. He has averaged at least five yards per carry over his last three games while handling at least 17 touches per contest, according to Sports Illustrated. Without the edge-setting of Sweat or the communication from Edwards, the defense is wide open. Even the gravity of Odeyingbo, which often forces double-teams on early downs, will be missing.

The Bears defense needs new heroes to show up. Austin Booker had a massive game against Green Bay with two sacks, three tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. He has to do it again to stop Robinson from running to the outside.

The depth chart is being tested like never before. Daniel Hardy is a top candidate to see more snaps since Sweat and Odeyingbo are out. Hardy got a multi-year extension in the offseason, and now he has to prove he can handle the edge. James Lynch could also help by providing a big body in the middle of the field. He is a strong run-stopper during his first year in Chicago.

There is also some hype around Jamree Kromah. He could get his first regular-season snap this Sunday. During the preseason, Kromah recorded three sacks, four tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. The defensive line is thin, and the team is relying on these unproven pieces to survive the Falcons.

The offense might get a boost, but the defense is struggling. Yahoo Sports reported that quarterback Caleb Williams practiced fully all week and is expected to be back in the lineup.

articles.title: Vani Kapoor’s biggest lesson is mental, not technical, ahead of Indian Women’s Open
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Vani Kapoor, the biggest change in her golf has not necessarily been technical. It has been learning to deal with herself on the course.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Vani Kapoor, the biggest change in her golf has not necessarily been technical. It has been learning to deal with herself on the course. Once driven heavily by results and hard on herself whenever she failed to win, the Indian golfer now believes in staying in the present, accepting mistakes and enjoying the process.The change, she explained, has come through small mental adjustments rather than a dramatic overhaul of her game.Ahead of the Indian Women’s Open at the DLF Golf and Country Club from Oct 22 to 25, she said, “I enjoy making mistakes. I learn from them. And the same way, I give myself credit when I play well. Previously, I wouldn't do that. These small mental habits have really helped me.”Vani believes that working consistently on her game and trusting the process have begun to reflect in her performances. With confidence growing, her focus is on maintaining that balance instead of becoming consumed by the prospect of winning.That approach will be tested at the Indian Women’s Open at the DLF Golf and Country Club, a venue she describes as the toughest course she has encountered across her playing experiences in Asia, Europe and the United States.“Over here, you need to be so accurate. You need to know where to make your mistakes. On other golf courses, you don't really think that way. You can't be so precise with your mistakes either, but this course really punishes you,” Vani said.She added, “The challenge extends beyond technical ability. Players must remain mentally composed through rounds that can last five to six hours, maintaining concentration across all 72 holes. On a course where errors can quickly prove costly, the ability to manage pressure could be as decisive as the quality of a player's ball-striking.”For Indian golfers, familiarity with the venue could offer an advantage against an international field featuring some of the world's leading players. Vani, however, cautioned that knowing the course does not automatically translate into success.She also believes the growing number of top-five and top-10 finishes by Indian women over the past five to 10 years reflects the improvement in the country's golf standards. Yet, the absence of an Indian winner at the tournament remains a significant talking point.“We Indians have had so many top-five and top-10 finishes in the last five to 10 years. The game has really improved. But the person who wins a trophy needs that luck. All 72 holes need to go according to them. Seventy-one holes are not enough,” she said.“Finishing second or third, the player is as good as the winner. But ultimately, there's only one person who takes the trophy. I really hope that an Indian wins it, and I hope even more that I win it,” she said.For Vani, the prospect of winning at home brings pressure, but she views it as something to embrace rather than resist. She credits the people around her for helping her remain calm and believes accepting the emotions that come with competition is essential to performing at her best.Winning this tournament remains the ultimate goal, but she is determined not to let that ambition dictate every moment of her tournament. Her priority is to focus on what she can control, trust the preparation and allow the result to follow.For a golfer who has spent years learning to be less consumed by the outcome, the challenge at DLF will be to combine that mental freedom with the precision the course demands. articles.title: Green Party leader Zack Polanski says he will not overturn Zionism motion
articles.summary: The Green Party leader said, while he wanted to amend it, the motion would stand until 2028.
articles.body:
Zack Polanski has said he will not overturn a motion passed by Green Party members that declared Zionism to be racist.

The party leader told the Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday programme that, while he would like to amend it, the motion would be party policy until 2028 and denied it was controversial.

The motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month, described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It divided the party and sparked a major backlash from MPs, Jewish campaigners, the government and the European Green movement.

The fallout from the motion overshadowed the final days of Polanski's campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, in which he came second to Labour, and threatened his leadership .

He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813, a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members.

Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

"At the first available opportunity, I do want to amend it - I want to move away from one state, towards saying that Israelis and Palestinians should decide that future for themselves."

He said this would not be until 2028 as "you can't [amend it] within the rules, so when you vote on something in our party conference that's then policy for two years".

Kuenssberg asked if he would therefore change the rules as leader, but Polanski said: "I think if members have made a decision, then I respect the democratic will of our members."

Polanski had previously said he would not have voted for the motion without amendments.

Green MPs, including Ellie Chowns, have called for the party's member-led decision-making procedures to be reviewed given how few people took part in the vote.

articles.title: Chacarra vence en India y quiere imitar a Seve y Rahm
articles.standfirst: El madrileño gana con autoridad, logra el reconocimiento mundial y persigue a falta de tres torneos el título final del European Tour, la Race to Dubái, que sólo los dos maestros han levantado entre los españoles
articles.summary: El madrileño gana con autoridad, logra el reconocimiento mundial y persigue a falta de tres torneos el título final del European Tour, la Race to Dubái, que sólo los dos maestros han levantado entre los españoles
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra se ha ganado definitivamente la admiración mundial. El madrileño de 26 años levantó el título del Dp World India Championship, la tercera victoria en 2026 tras los triunfos en el KLM Open y el Open de Italia. Además, pasa a lidera la Race to Dubai -la Orden de Mérito de toda la vida- a falta de tres torneos, por delante de Patrick Reed y Rory McIlroy, dos ganadores de Majors. Fue el primer español en ganar en el LIV Golf, en octubre en 2022 en Tailandia. Y ahora persigue algo más importante: ganar la general del DP World Tour como sólo han hecho Seve Ballesteros y Jon Rahm, dos tótem de la historia del golf español, dos de los cinco golfistas que han ganado tres torneos o más en una misma temporada junto a José María Olazábal, Sergio García y Miguel Ángel Jiménez. Chacarra también está ya en ese grupo. Su triunfo en Nueva Delhi, el segundo que logra en India en su carrera, lo reivindica como un grandísimo golfista, que el año que viene en el PGA Tour no será un jugador más que intenta las Américas. Tiene pinta de que peleará más de una semana por la victoria en el circuito más afamado. Quienes denostaban victorias como la lograda en el LIV Golf, porque era a 54 hoyos, o en un Tour algo menor como el Asian Tour, ya no pondrán un pero. No son sus tres victorias anteriores en el DP World Tour con 'fields' de jugadores que estaban por debajo del top 50 mundial. En India ha batido al número 2 del mundo, McIlroy; el número 6, Tommy Fleetwood. El 18, Justin Rose. Y a tres de los cuatro ganadores de Grandes de esta temporada. (Resultados) La victoria el domingo, soleado, sin viento, un campo estrecho y un rough considerable, lo hizo en dos sesiones. En realidad, en una. Al alba reanudó la tercera vuelta que no había podido concluir el sábado y ahí sentenció el torneo. En los siete hoyos que faltaban hizo tres birdies y un eagle, con un chip en el 18, para una tarjeta de 63 golpes. Acabada la vuelta, en 19 bajo par, tenía cinco golpes de ventaja sobre el neozelandés Hillier, el que la semana pasada en Madrid se llevó un BMW por hacer un hoyo en uno. Los últimos 18 hoyos, que comenzaron con otro birdie de Chacarra, tuvieron la tensión del desenlace y los nervios finales. La diferencia respecto a sus perseguidores llegó a ser de seis golpes y no bajó de dos nunca, la renta con la que ganó tras 70 golpes, en un torneo que también fue provechoso para Ángel Hidalgo, tercero. El último trecho del año está ofreciendo la imagen real del potencial del ganador del Open de España de 2024. Fue segundo en Francia y cuarto en Suiza. Se le torció el hoyo 16 con un doble bogey y eso le quitó el subcampeonato. Y lo mejor es que Eugenio sabe que tiene mejora. Apenas ha cogido un 60 por ciento de calles esta semana. No es la estadística que más pesa en estos tiempos, y menos en campos poco castigadores como los que se encontrará la mayoría de citas el próximo año. Pero estar en la hierba corta permite mover la bola a tu antojo. Su fortaleza, en cambio, es cómo juega los hierros, lo que le hace liderar las estadísticas de greenes cogidos. Y cómo patea. Usa el de escoba, que estéticamente es horrible, pero le saca la efectividad que sólo Bernhard Langer le ha sacado históricamente a ese tipo de palo. El trabajo de Alejandro Larrazábal como entrenador desde hace año y medio es excepcional. Como añadido, juega a toda velocidad. Digno del mejor aplauso. Chacarra, en fin, entra, además, entre los 40 mejores jugadores del mundo por primera vez en su carrera. Se garantiza, de paso, ser invitado al Masters de Augusta, lo que supondrá que en 2027 jugará los cuatro grandes en el mismo curso, algo inédito también en su carrera. Y se posiciona muy bien para la Ryder Cup de Adare Manor, otro objetivo prioritario para un jugador que es un tremendo competidor. Elogiable después de haber pasado por un tiempo en el que se vio perdido mentalmente y optó por parar.

articles.title: Man arrested after boy, 16, dies in Birmingham crash
articles.summary: The 19-year-old man is held on suspicion of causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving.
articles.body:
A man has been arrested after a 16-year-old boy was killed in a crash in Birmingham.

Police said the teenager was in a white Seat Ibiza which was understood to have hit railings on Shaftmoor Lane at about 20:30 BST on Saturday.

A second passenger, a boy in his teens, was taken to hospital with a serious arm injury.

A 19-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving and failing to provide a breath specimen, West Midlands Police said.

The force stated the 16-year-old boy who lost his life was pronounced dead at the scene, in the Acocks Green area, despite the best efforts of paramedics.

It appealed for information, adding specialist officers from the serious collision investigation unit were asking anyone who had dashcam footage from around the time of the crash to get in touch.

articles.title: DP World India Championship: Eugenio Chacarra wins to move top of Race to Dubai standings with Rory McIlroy finishing in a share of 42nd place
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra completes third win of DP World Tour season with victory in Delhi; Rory McIlroy shoots two-over final round as he finishes joint-42nd and slips to third in Race to Dubai; watch Genesis Championship live on Sky Sports from 4am Thursday
articles.body:
Chacarra carded a two-under 70 in New Delhi to reach 21 under as he followed his back-to-back triumphs in June at the KLM Open in Amsterdam and the Italian Open in Turin with another success and secured a fourth DP World Tour title overall having clamed his maiden win at the 2025 Hero Indian Open.

The former LIV player, who took a five-stroke lead into the final round following a nine-under 63 in round three, picked up shots at two of his first three holes before a bogey at six and some clutch par putts preceded a birdie at 11.

Pressure was applied by Australia's Daniel Hillier (19 under) - when Hillier birdied the last, Chacarra's advantage was cut to two with three holes remaining - Chacarra's fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo (15 under) and Poland's Adrian Meronk (15 under) but the leader held firm to reach 4,092.89 points in the Race to Dubai.

The 26-year-old, who has knocked Reed off top spot for the first time in seven months, could become the third Spaniard, after Jon Rahm (2019) and six-time winner Seve Ballesteros, to be crowned Europe's No 1 golfer.

Chacarra said afterwards: "I know what I'm capable of. I was one of the best amateurs in the world and I want to be one of the best professional players in the world.

"It would mean the world to [win the Race to Dubai]. Rahm and Seve are heroes for me. Seve did everything for European and Spanish golf and Rahm is a guy I look up to.

"Hopefully I can put my name on that trophy, too."

Where did Reed and McIlroy finish in Delhi?

Reed (eight under) and McIlroy (four under) finished joint-23rd and joint-42nd respectively in India.

The major winners sit second and third in the Race to Dubai standings, with Casey Jarvis and Aaron Rai rounding out the top five ahead of next week's Genesis Championship in South Korea.

The tour is set to move to the United Arab Emirates for the final two tournaments - the Abu Dhabi Championship from November 5 and the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai a week later.

McIroy, looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Race to Dubai titles, began his final round in Delhi 13 shots back after completing an even-par third round of 72 earlier on Sunday, with play having been halted on Saturday evening due to fading light.

The world No 2 got off to a promising start in his closing round, birdieing the par-five first, only to then double bogey three and drop another shot at four before a birdie at eight was followed by a bogey to finish his front nine.

McIlroy registered two birdies and two bogeys coming home, with a gain at the par-five 18th seeing him sign for a two-over 74.

The 37-year-old, who will not play in South Korea next week, said: "It was great to be back in India. I wish I had played better but I'll go home for a couple of weeks, sharpen up and get myself ready for the last few events.

"I didn't really touch a club after [the BMW PGA Championship in September] until I turned up this week. I didn't feel I was at my sharpest, so looking forward to practising. Eugenio is playing well. That makes my job a bit harder going into the last two events."

Reed, aiming to become the second American after Collin Morikawa in 2021 to pick up the Race to Dubai, rounded off his week with a three-under 69.

Chacarra: Two of the best are coming for me now

Chacarra is now in pole position to claim the Harry Vardon Trophy in a season in which his three victories have come around five other top-five finishes, including tied-second at last week's Open de Espana in his native Madrid.

The Spaniard added on pursuing the Race to Dubai crown: "It is not going to be easy.

"Rory always plays good in Dubai, so it will be a big battle. Patrick, too - two of the best players in the world are coming for me."

England's Tommy Fleetwood notched a top-five in India with a final-round, four-under 68 elevating him to 13 under, while Scotland's Robert MacIntyre and Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin ended up in the top 10 on 12 under.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy explains why he played in India after PGA Tour player Kevin Kisner accused him of chasing reported $10m appearance fee
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy defends his participation in the DP World India Championship amid accusations from Kevin Kisner about chasing a $10 million appearance fee, emphasizing his commitment to promoting golf in India.
articles.body: Rory McIlroy travelled to New Delhi for the inaugural DP World India Championship, a $4 million event intended to bring golf to a major new audience. But his appearance also prompted a blunt accusation from fellow PGA Tour member Kevin Kisner, who suggested McIlroy was there primarily for a reported $10 million appearance fee. McIlroy has now answered that criticism, defending both the financial realities of professional golf and his interest in growing the game in India.McIlroy’s India appearance drew criticism from KisnerMcIlroy made his first appearance in India at the DP World India Championship, held at Delhi Golf Club from October 16–19, 2026. The Northern Irishman arrived among a strong field that included Justin Rose, Tommy Fleetwood, Shane Lowry and Patrick Reed, with the event offering a reported $4 million prize fund.His participation came shortly after he signed a multi-year deal to become global golf ambassador for DP World, the UAE logistics company that became the European Tour’s title sponsor in November 2021. Announcing the partnership, McIlroy said: “That’s why I’m proud to announce I’m joining DP World as Global Golf Ambassador. Excited to push the boundaries of performance together, backed by world-leading smart end-to-end logistics.”McIlroy has spoken about taking golf into new markets, but Kisner questioned whether that was the real motivation behind the trip. Speaking on the Fore Play Podcast, the four-time PGA Tour winner, now NBC’s lead golf analyst, said McIlroy was reportedly receiving $10 million to compete.“That is such a dog s*** comment, but I guess for the right price we could all say that comment,” Kisner said. “He doesn’t want to globally expand in India; he wants to get his $10 million bucks and go play in India.”Kisner also questioned the tournament’s location and McIlroy’s decision to leave his driver out of his equipment for the week.“I know there’s a pile of guys that got paid for that event. How else would you get that event in India with eight billion people in the middle of the city?” he said. “And Rory’s not even hitting a driver this week. You think he wants to go play a tournament where he can’t use his No. 1 weapon? So give me a break.”He went further, suggesting players were expected to deliver prepared comments about expanding golf internationally.“They always seem to say the right things while they’re over there,” Kisner said. “As part of your appearance fee, ‘Here’s your script for altruism, and you need to mention these four lines in whatever interview you do throughout the week,’ which is totally fine, I’d do it too, and all of us on this podcast would.”Kisner added that he found it “very odd” that players would travel to India for a course where McIlroy could not use his driver, rather than play what he described as “the sickest course in the world”.McIlroy says the financial and sporting reasons can coexistMcIlroy said he had not seen Kisner’s comments when reporters asked him about them in New Delhi, and questioned why his participation had prompted such a response.“I didn’t see that. I don’t know why me being in India would make Kis need to comment on that,” McIlroy said.He did not deny that players can receive appearance fees, but rejected the idea that payment necessarily undermines their wider reasons for competing.“Two things can be true at the same time,” McIlroy said. “People can get paid to come and play at a tournament, but at the same time, do it from a place of a genuine interest of trying to bring the sport to another country, a developing country, a country where the middle class in India is larger than the whole population of the United States. It’s a huge market for golf.”McIlroy has long been among golf’s most prominent international figures, competing across the United States, England, Scotland, Ireland, Australia, Dubai and India during 2026. His trip to New Delhi also placed him among the headline players promoting a tournament designed to expand the sport’s reach.A disappointing finish followed a promising startMcIlroy’s week did not produce the result he wanted. He began with an eagle and also made an impressive bunker-shot eagle on the 14th, but lost ground during the third round after several bogeys and a double bogey left him well behind the leaders.He finished tied for 42nd at four-under par after closing with a two-over 74, ending 17 strokes behind winner Eugenio Lopez-Chacarra. The Spaniard finished at 21-under, winning by two shots and moving ahead of Patrick Reed at the top of the Race to Dubai standings.McIlroy had arrived in India chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, having entered the tournament one win short of Colin Montgomerie’s record. His result leaves that pursuit on hold, with the DP World Tour playoffs beginning next month in Abu Dhabi.The inaugural championship’s prize money also placed McIlroy’s reported appearance fee in perspective, although the $10 million figure cited by Kisner was separate from the tournament’s official purse. The winner received $680,000, with $440,000 for second place and $252,000 for third.McIlroy is expected to return to action in Abu Dhabi next month as he begins the DP World Tour playoffs and continues his bid for an eighth Race to Dubai crown. articles.body: Golfer Hailey Ostrom will never be accused of being unable to multitask. Not when she has multiple defenses of summer in a bikini armed with her golf club under her belt. And not when she's hitting the golf course out in Arizona in the middle of her 31 days of Halloween costumes either. Which, unlike Paige Spiranac, I'm happy to report she is still doing. I put my Big J suspenders on for this one. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I thought I remembered seeing Hailey's Halloween announcement earlier this month, but I wanted to confirm that it was indeed from this year after seeing her smashing golf balls on an Arizona course. Sometimes you get wrapped up in things and your focus turns toward other types of content. I wouldn’t go as far as saying that I doubted Hailey Ostrom's ability to multitask. That didn’t happen. I thought perhaps she could have shifted her focus, as it appears Paige has done. Now to be fair to Paige, she did hit the golf course recently in an interesting Willy Wonka Halloween costume. However, her annual 31 days of churning out Halloween costumes appears to have come to an end. articles.summary: Rory McIlroy fired back at Kevin Kisner's claim that his DP World India Championship appearance was purely driven by a hefty appearance fee.
articles.body: Four-time PGA Tour winner Kevin Kisner accused Rory McIlroy of not exactly being genuine about growing the game of golf while teeing it up in India on the DP World Tour. Now, McIlroy has issued a rebuttal to Kisner's harsh accusations. In the lead-up to the DP World India Championship, McIlroy appeared at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi and, among the many topics he touched on, explained that he hoped his decision to play in the event would help promote and grow the game in India. While his comments were as generic as they come, Kisner didn't buy them and called the six-time major winner out directly. Kisner claimed the only reason McIlroy was playing in India was to collect a hefty appearance fee. RORY MCILROY ADMITS HE'S NOT INTERESTED IN PLAYING MOST PGA TOUR EVENTS MOVING FORWARD "That is such a dog sh-t comment, but I guess for the right price, we could all say that comment," Kisner said on the Fore Play podcast. "He doesn’t want to globally expand in India; he wants to get his 10 million bucks and go play in India." "They always seem to say the right things while they’re over there," Kisner later continued. "As part of your appearance fee, here’s your script for altruism, and you need to mention these four lines in whatever interview you do throughout the week. Which is totally fine, I’d do it too, and all of us on this podcast would. I just find it hilarious when you can pop up and play an event where Rory McIlroy can’t hit his driver, and all those guys show up, and nobody’s like, ‘alright, this is stupid’, whenever they can go play the sickest course in the world, and none of them show up. It’s just very odd to me." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! McIlroy, who finished T-42 in the India event, was asked about Kisner's remarks after Sunday's final round, and while he explained that he had not seen them beforehand, he reacted candidly. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "I didn't see that. I don't know why me being in India would make Kis need to comment on that," McIlroy told The Mirror. "Two things can be true at the same time. People can get paid to come and play at a tournament, but at the same time, do it from a place of a genuine interest in trying to bring the sport to another country, a developing country, a country where the middle class in India is larger than the whole population of the United States. It's a huge market for golf." McIlroy explaining that two things can be true at once certainly applies here, and his admission that he was paid an appearance fee to play in the event is completely transparent. The same can be said for Kisner, who admitted that he'd show up and play in a tournament too if it came with a guaranteed payday.

articles.title: Trump Shuttering Popular D.C. Golf Course For 15 Month Renovation
articles.summary: The president said the new course will be open to the public but capable of hosting “World Class Tournaments.”
articles.body:
East Potomac Golf Links, a highly popular municipal golf course in Washington, D.C., and the target of one of President Donald Trump's contentious renovation projects, will close for 15 months starting in November, the president said on Sunday.

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump shared a map of the redesigned course, which he said would be "open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments."

The "current Course" will close when renovations begin on Nov. 15, Trump said, and will reopen in "approximately 15 months."

The announcement comes shortly after the National Park Service cut down hundreds of trees at the course, a move that prompted a federal judge to block further tree removal and chastise lawyers for the Trump administration.

430. That's how many healthy, non-invasive trees were removed from the East Potomac Golf Links in a few hours last week, the Trump administration acknowledged. "Breakneck speed to clear trees that posed no harm," District Court Judge Ana Reyes wrote in a memo accompanying an order to stop cutting down any tree at the course until Oct. 26. "The reason? Disputed. The budget? Unclear. The environmental impact? Unstudied. The urgency? None. Next steps: bulldoze hundreds more."

Days after the order was signed, the Trump administration moved to disqualify Reyes from presiding over the case, claiming she "hamstrung the Government's legitimate attempts to maintain East Potomac Park" and accused her of being biased against the Trump administration. "More than being upset and furious right now, I am just deeply disappointed in the government," Reyes reportedly told Justice Department lawyers at a hearing. When one attorney told the judge the government had done its best to gather information about the tree removal project, Reyes reportedly responded with: "You did not do your best. You did ⁠your absolute worst."

Trump previously announced work would begin on renovating the golf course in September. The current course has two nine-hold courses for easier difficulty levels, one par 72 18-hole course, and a mini-golf course. Green fees max out at $48 for the 18-hole course on weekends and holidays, but the easier courses cost even less. Trump, who is an avid golfer and investor in high-end golf clubs like his Trump Doral in Miami and Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster, New Jersey, said he planned to replace the municipal course with a "championship-level" course. In his post on Sunday, Trump doubled down on this promise, writing the "United States Golf Association, PGA of America, and the PGA Tour have already been notified that they will soon have one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World to put on their list of great places to play, and hold Major Events." During his second term in office, Trump has been increasingly concerned with renovation projects and new monuments around the national capital, including building a new White House ballroom, a triumphal arch and renovating the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

articles.title: Race to Dubai: Eugenio Chacarra seals two-stroke win in India to lead standings from Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra wins the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.
articles.body:
DP World India Championship, round four leaderboard

21 E Chacarra (Spa), -19 D Hillier (NZ), -15 A Hidalgo (Spa), A Meronk (Pol), -13 J Luiten (Ned), JC Ritchie (SA), T Fleetwood (Eng), G de Leo (Ita)

Selected others: -12 R MacIntyre (Sco), T McKibbin (NI), - 10 S Lowry (Ire), -9 A Rai (Eng), -8 P Reed (USA), -4 R McIlroy (NI), J Rose (Eng)

Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.

Spain's Chacarra finished on 21 under, with American Reed and world number two McIlroy well off the pace by the final round of this event.

After opening with successive scores of 67 in his first two rounds at Delhi Golf Club, bad light halted play with Chacarra still on the 11th hole of his third round on Saturday.

That left the 26-year-old with extra work on Sunday and he concluded his third round with a five-shot lead after a nine-under 63.

A two-under 70 in his final round was then enough to see off the challenge of New Zealand's Daniel Hillier who birdied the last to put the pressure on the victor.

The win was Chacarra's third of the season as he looks to emulate Jon Rahm and Seve Ballesteros to become the third Spaniard to top the season-long standings on the DP World Tour.

"Those two guys are heroes for me as a Spanish golfer," Chacarra told Sky Sports.

"Seve did everything for European and Spanish golf, and then Jon, it's a guy that I've been looking up to since he went to college and professional golf. What he has accomplished, it's amazing.

"Hopefully I can put my name on that trophy too. That's one of the goals."

Reed, the Masters champion of 2018, had led the way since March after early-season victories in Qatar and Dubai, but he has been overhauled with just three events remaining before the winner is crowned next month.

A final-round 69 in Delhi meant Reed finished on eight under and in a tie for 23rd, while McIlroy was four shots further back with his disappointing weekend only good enough for a share of 42nd.

The 37-year-old from Northern Ireland was playing this event for the second consecutive year and started solidly before a two-over 74 in his concluding round.

McIlroy's compatriot Tom McKibbin fared better at 12 under, a score that was good enough for ninth place alongside Scotland's Robert MacIntyre. Belgium's Thomas Detry and United Arab Emirates' Adrian Otaegui.

articles.title: New fluorescent sensors help scientists monitor acidity changes inside cancer cells
articles.summary: Scientists developed dual-colour fluorescent sensors to track pH changes in cancer cell mitochondria and lysosomes, improving compartment-specific acidity imaging.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Researchers, including a scientist from Hyderabad’s Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), have developed and studied two fluorescent sensors that can track acidity levels inside cancer cells, offering a new way to understand changes in cellular compartments linked to disease.By producing different colour signals, the sensors can simultaneously identify where they are inside a cell and measure the acidity of their surroundings.The findings, published in ‘Scientific Reports’ on Oct 13, compare two dual-colour sensors, one based on red-blue fluorescence and the other on red-green fluorescence. The researchers tested the sensors in laboratory solutions and HeLa cancer cells and compared their performance with commonly used cellular markers, MitoTracker and LysoTracker.Tracking acidityThe sensors were designed to target mitochondria and lysosomes, two cellular compartments that operate under very different pH conditions. While lysosomes are highly acidic, mitochondria function in relatively neutral to basic environments.Monitoring these pH differences can help scientists better understand how cells function and how changes in acidity are associated with diseases, including cancer.Both sensors use a piperazine unit to target specific cellular compartments. The red-blue sensor combines pyrene with a rhodamine dye, while the red-green version links naphthalimide to rhodamine.Under acidic conditions, the rhodamine component produces a red fluorescent signal. In mitochondria, the sensors emit either blue or green fluorescence, whereas in acidic lysosomes they generate combined blue-red or green-red signals. This enables researchers to visualise compartment-specific acidity within the same cell.The blue and green fluorescent components also allow the sensors to detect pH changes beyond pH 6, extending their sensing range.Improving cellular imagingThe sensors work through a combination of electron transfer, charge transfer and energy transfer mechanisms between their fluorescent components. Researchers evaluated their behaviour across a range of neutral-to-acidic environments and calculated four different pKa values for the red-green sensor, providing a detailed measure of its acid-base responsiveness.The study notes that analysing ratios between fluorescence signals helps minimise errors caused by differences in illumination or sensor concentration, making measurements more reliable.The researchers describe the molecules as valuable tools for studying pH-related changes tied to cellular function and disease. The experiments reported in the study were conducted in laboratory solutions and cultured cells.The authors include Akshita, Garima Tiwari, Rythem Goyal, Saleem Javed, Shruti Mishra, Swati Singh, Payel Roy, Rajesh Kumar, Priyanka Srivastava, Vikram Singh and Ute Resch-Genger. articles.title: Eugenio Chacarra shares what he thinks about his time on LIV Golf now after winning again on the DP World Tour
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra has insisted that he remains grateful to LIV Golf after winning for a third time this season on the DP World Tour in India on Sunday. Chacar...
articles.body:
Eugenio Chacarra has insisted that he remains grateful to LIV Golf after winning for a third time this season on the DP World Tour in India on Sunday.

Chacarra is set to secure his ticket to the PGA Tour in some style at the end of the season. The Spaniard now leads the Race to Dubai after clinching the DP World India Championship this week.

It is the 26-year-old's third win of the campaign. He has now moved ahead of Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai, while he will have an opportunity to extend his lead over the American and Rory McIlroy when he plays in the Genesis Championship next week.

Eugenio Chacarra reflects on his time with LIV Golf

It has been a remarkable journey for Eugenio Chacarra , with many golf fans becoming aware of his talent when he decided to sign with LIV Golf in 2022.

He ended up leaving LIV after the 2024 season, eventually earning his place on the DP World Tour . It could be argued that joining LIV and leaving when he did set him back in his quest to become a top player.

However, speaking after his win at Delhi Golf Club, Chacarra claimed that he reflects on time with LIV extremely positively.

"Yeah, when I left LIV I wanted to be in majors, be in Ryder Cups, win tournaments on the DP World Tour, be on the PGA Tour . That's what I dreamt of since I was little," he said.

"Obviously when I grew up LIV wasn't in existence, but when LIV came up, as one of the best amateurs in the world they offered me something that I couldn't say no to. I'm very thankful for that. My time there was great.

"It helped a lot of things for my career. I can have a great team surrounding me thanks to LIV. I can travel a little better. I can go to nicer hotels. I can give my family and my future family a great life.

"So I'm always grateful to LIV. Nothing bad to say. My time was done. Decided with my team and family that the next step was ready for me.

"Like I said, I believe in myself. I believe I can be one of the best players in the world, and that's what I wake up every single morning dreaming, of being one of the best players in the world, and like you said contending in majors.

"Hopefully this will move me up pretty good on the ranking and I could be confirmed for next year's four majors. It will be my first Masters and I am lucky now that I played the other three. Last year was my first Open. I enjoyed every single moment of it. I played four days, and I think I can, with my game, keep working hard to be contending in those tournaments in a couple years or next year."

What Eugenio Chacarra was the only player to do in LIV Golf history until the league's final event of this season

Chacarra very nearly ended up in a unique position when it came to LIV 1.0.

The Spaniard secured his first professional win in the LIV event in Bangkok back in 2022. Funnily enough, he finished that event three shots ahead of Patrick Reed in Thailand.

For a long time, Chacarra was the only player to have secured his first ever professional victory in a LIV Golf event. His victory should have arguably shown the league a potential way forward, with some of the young players in their ranks having real potential.

However, they spent too long focusing on the big money signings, who, ultimately, did not help LIV establish itself as a consistent rival to the PGA Tour.

The only other player to win a first professional title in a LIV event ended up being Michael La Sasso, with the 22-year-old clinching a victory in Indianapolis.

It still remains to be seen whether that proves to be the last ever LIV Golf event.
